text:
Carolina arrives in Winnipeg as the better team by the underlying numbers. The Hurricanes generate 3.94 expected goals per 60 and allow 2.44, and they have taken 58% of the expected goals at five on five. The Jets sit at 2.94 for and 3.30 against, with 46% at five on five. The model projects 3.48 goals for CAR tonight against 2.64 for WPG. Carolina's power play creates 1.0 expected goals a game, well ahead of Winnipeg's 0.67, though CAR takes 4.75 penalties a game, which keeps feeding the other side's power play.

Form favors the visitors too. CAR is 5-0-0 in its last five and had more expected goals in all five, averaging 63%. WPG is 3-1-1 in its last five, with 48% of the expected goals, and played last night in Chicago (a 4-3 overtime loss), so the Jets have one day of rest to Carolina's three. Both teams are missing key forwards and defensemen (Taylor Hall and Jordan Staal for CAR, Josh Morrissey for WPG), and the model prices those absences. In net, projected starters Brandon Bussi (CAR) and Clay Stevenson (WPG) are both shaky this season, at -1.95 and -0.72 goals saved above expected. Last year Bussi was at +1.15 over 39 games, and Stevenson at +3.1 over just four.

Kyle Connor is the Jets' best bet, with a 40% chance to score and 11 points in seven games, though he is flagged as due to cool. For Carolina, Andrei Svechnikov (40% to score, top power play) and Sebastian Aho (69% to record a point) lead the way, and Mark Jankowski has goals in five straight. Nino Niederreiter is one point from 500, a milestone the model doesn't price.
